summary: Marks bars that poke past a recent swing high or low on a volume spike and close back inside, with a line from the swing.
overview: Stop Runs / Sweeps marks bars that trade beyond a recent swing high or low, on unusually high volume, and then close back inside. A small triangle sits at the wick, a dotted line runs from the swing to the sweep, and a short label names it. Swing highs swept are red and swing lows swept are green.
how: A swing high or low is the extreme of 5 bars on each side. A sweep needs volume of at least 1.5 times the 20-bar average. Swings older than 300 bars are ignored.
It uses traded volume where order flow exists and the chart's own volume on other symbols, so it works anywhere bars have volume.
use: Some traders watch sweeps of swing highs or lows as places where stops may have been run.
Use the line to see which swing was taken.
Some traders combine sweeps with absorption or delta to see what happened at the sweep.
notes: On futures charts use Stop Runs (L2); a saved futures chart that still holds this one is switched to it automatically. Crypto charts keep this one.
A sweep is a past pattern, not a forecast.
